title: Memory Has to Be a Service, Not a Chat
description: I am adding thought capture, branches, cost routing, and tools so an agent can keep working without treating the conversation as the store.
body:
An agent that can only remember inside the current conversation will forget the work the moment the window closes. That is not a small inconvenience. It is the same failure as putting the filing cabinet inside the assistant. The next session starts from zero, and the last decision has no record a later reader can inspect.

Today I add a working memory service. Thoughts can be captured, searched, listed, and resolved. Branches can be opened, closed, and recalled. A cost router estimates spend and lists models against a daily cap. The MCP surface grows from the original five tools to a thought group, a branch group, and a cost group. The command line grows a thought family: capture, search, recent, actions, resolve, patterns, synthesize. The point is not to declare every saved thought useful. It is to give memory an operational surface.

The wrong default

The usual agent stack treats context as a disposable prompt. Useful remarks evaporate. Unresolved actions live in the scrollback. Cost is someone else’s problem. VALESKA already indexes files. It now has to index the working notes of the people and agents who use those files, without pretending a note is a fact about the enterprise.

A logbook is not the ship. It is how the next watch knows what was tried. Thoughts here are typed — insight, decision, action, and the rest of the schema — and they embed into the same vector store the files use. Branches are a way to keep an investigation from contaminating the main line. None of that replaces judgment about a business. It keeps the evidence that judgment used.

What is actually on the bench

The services and tests land in this commit. The thought schema and a project-state graph schema had been written in the days before; this commit does not, by itself, prove those migrations have been applied in every environment. Contradiction detection and entity search are not in this drop. There is no Alfresco in this drop. A StoryTeller router stub exists and is not the memory service.

Nineteen tools on the MCP surface is a count, not a personality. Five of them are still the November file tools. The rest are how an agent writes a note, follows a branch, and asks what the day has cost before it spends again. If those calls are not used, the service is furniture.

The cost router is a budget and a registry of models, not a claim that one vendor is the classification engine. The default daily cap is a dollar. That is a control, not a performance promise. Tests cover the Second Brain MVP and the cost router. They are the evidence that the surface can be constructed and checked, not that every agent in the house already writes through it.

The next test

The next work is whether a thought captured in one session can be retrieved in the next, with its type and its unresolved action still attached, without overstating what the system knows. Until that is ordinary practice, this is a service we can call, not a mind.

Historical basis: VALESKA commit 1bf9aea, March 6, 2026; contemporaneous Second Brain services, MCP tool registration, CLI thought commands, and the Second Brain and cost-router test suites. Thought and project-state SQL files predate this commit and are not treated as proven-applied by it.

data.author: David Gargan
data.coverAlt: A great scroll of recorded work unrolling into branching paths through a moonlit archive: memory as a service an agent can capture and retrieve, not a conversation that evaporates.
